newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Africa calls on EU to help solve debt crisis.
newsitem.headline: Africa calls on EU to help solve debt crisis.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity has appealed to the European Union to help resolve a debt crisis affecting the 70-member African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) group of countries, the EU's trading partners.

In a report tabled at a meeting of African ambassadors preparing for an OAU summit in Zimbabwe next week, the OAU said Africa had an unmanageable external debt of around $400 billion. But it gave no figure for the whole ACP group.
"The debt service is crippling and robbing the economy of needed resources for development. The EU should recognise the need to formulate concrete options for tackling the ACP debt crisis," it said.
The report also called on the EU to help strengthen the ACP states' general economic capacity, saying this has become more urgent in the face of the globalisation of the world economy.
Africa's trade with the EU, it said, had fallen in 1994 to 2.8 percent of the EU's total trade with the rest of the world from 6.7 percent in 1976.
